summary: Implemented the playable synthetic CareLink ride lifecycle across the direct Transportation dashboard and shared FLOW state: request, primary assignment and failure, backup recovery, required logistics, versioned caregiver seen and patient acknowledgment, failure invalidation, no-option risk, isolated historical replay, minimized role views, and a truthful Uber Health integration-ready preview that is explicitly not connected.

commands: RED: npm run test:smoke -- tests/access.test.tsx (expected failure before the Transportation dashboard was wired)
npm run test:smoke (18 files, 90 tests passed)
npm run build (TypeScript and Vite production build passed)
npm run test:e2e (9 Chromium journeys passed)
RIDE browser inspection at 1440px and 375px (no horizontal overflow, no console errors, zero Uber requests)
tests.notes: The Transportation login now opens CareLink Transportation Workspace rather than Resource Directory. The committed desktop/mobile captures show the recovered v2 plan, failed primary retained beside the current backup, provider readiness cards, replay controls, required logistics, and truthful demo-only labels.

notes_for_next_agent: Uber Health remains presentation-only and has no reducer action, API request, booking path, contract claim, or success state.
CareLink provider, driver, trip, time, map, and contact values are synthetic scenario data; the selected map is static and does not represent live GPS.
Security review is not required by the approved LOW-risk frontend-only architecture.
